answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm fabricated work or coordinated abuse. A reputation-weighted random sample of tasks is checked against evidence, and penalties are shared with auditors only after agreement, limiting cheap collusion. A Sybil farm must lock capital across many accounts and risks losing it, while honest agents recover their stake; the terrace of accounts gains no extra influence without costly, verifiable performance, and a ridge of suspicious links can trigger deeper audits as a warning signal.
